subject: ACME - Audit logging discovery follow-up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: John Smith <john.smith@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: ACME - Audit logging discovery follow-up

Hi John / Olivia,

Great talking earlier. Per our call, I wanted to recap the audit-logging items ACME mentioned and propose next steps so we can size the ingest & retention needs for Dedicated/Private options. Key notes from the call: 

- Scope: admin activity logs (console, RBAC changes), API request/response logs, and SDK client usage.
- Retention target: 1 year standard, options to export to customer S3 (long-term) for 7+ years.
- Immutability: need for tamper-evident export and signed delivery for audits.
- Access controls: granular role-based access and read-only audit views for auditors.
- Regulatory flags: potential GDPR data subject requests and HIPAA applicability for a subset of logs.

Action items we agreed on: 
1) I'll share a short doc with our audit logging capabilities and format examples.
2) ACME to send the vendor security questionnaire, if you prefer, we can start by filling the SOC 2 / logging sections.
3) Loop in our security lead (Neha) for any technical deep dives on immutability/export.

Attached: redwood_audit_logging_overview.pdf (high-level format + export options).

Next availability: I have 30 minutes Tue/Wed morning PST for a follow-up to go over the questionnaire and a sample export. Let me know what works.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_audit_logging_overview.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: John Smith <john.smith@acme.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME - Audit logging discovery follow-up

Thanks Aditya, this is helpful. A couple of clarifying Qs from our security/compliance side before we schedule the follow-up: 

1) SOC 2: do you have a SOC 2 Type II report available for 2026? If not, what is the expected timeline to complete Type II?
2) Export: can exports be automatically delivered to our S3 with object locking enabled (for retention/immutability)?
3) PII in logs: what's your recommended approach to handle PII in API logs (masking vs redaction vs tokenization)?
4) Vendor questionnaire: attaching our standard security questionnaire, can you have your team start the logging & encryption sections?

We'd like to get the questionnaire back to procurement by end of next week if possible. 

John
John Smith
Director, IT Security
ACME Corp.
[attachment: acme_vendor_questionnaire.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: John Smith <john.smith@acme.com>, Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME - Audit logging discovery follow-up

John, thanks for the questions and the questionnaire. Quick answers below; Neha is cc'd for any technical clarifications we should add to the questionnaire responses. We can draft the pull-out answers and send back a PDF by EOD Thursday to hit your procurement timeline.

1) SOC 2: Redwood completed a SOC 2 Type II assessment for the 12-month period ending 2026-12-31. The report is available under NDA, we can provide it to procurement/legal.

2) Export & immutability: Yes, we support direct S3 exports. For immutability, we can deliver objects with headers compatible with S3 Object Lock (WORM) and provide signed manifests for export batches. For long-term legal hold, customers typically combine S3 Object Lock with our signed delivery and audit manifests.

3) PII handling: We recommend a layered approach: configurable masking at ingestion (PII redaction on fields), tokenization for derived identifiers, and keeping full raw logs encrypted-at-rest with KMS access controls. We'll include recommended config examples in the questionnaire response.

4) Questionnaire: attaching an initial draft and pulling Neha in to review the technical responses.

Proposed next step: 30-min call Tues 10:00 AM PST to walk the export manifest example and SOC 2 delivery process. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Aditya
[attachment: redwood_audit_logging_overview.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, John Smith <john.smith@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME - Audit logging discovery follow-up

Looping in a short technical note:

- SOC 2: Confirming Aditya's note, we have a SOC 2 Type II report for 2026 (security and availability controls). We'll prepare the cover letter for procurement and include the test period.
- Exports: audit logs are exportable as newline-delimited JSON with per-file SHA256 and a signed manifest. We support S3 PutObject with SSE-KMS and can set Object Lock x-amz-object-lock-mode on delivery if ACME's bucket supports it.
- Immutability: Recommended pattern: enable S3 Object Lock + our signed manifests + store manifests in customer-controlled bucket with restricted KMS key. We can also support periodic Merkle-tree snapshots for additional tamper-evidence on request.
- API log schema: sample fields we'll include: timestamp, request_id, user_id (tokenized), endpoint, status_code, request_size, response_size, error_trace (redacted).

I'll review the questionnaire and add short technical responses to the logging & encryption sections; we should be able to return a cleaned PDF by Thu EOD.

-Neha
Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
